text.p: A Sicilian court on Tuesday sentenced 38 Mafiosi to a total of 328 years in jail in the final stage of a lengthy trial begun by assassinated judges Giovanni Falcone and Paolo Borsellino more than a decade ago.

The court in Palermo reached its verdict after 18 hours of deliberation on a range of cases, including the so-called Pizza Connection heroin smuggling ring and the stage-managed kidnapping of Sicilian banker Michele Sindona.

Among those sentenced were Vito and Leonardo Badalamenti, sons of jailed Mafia boss Gaetano Badalamenti who is serving a 45-year term in New Jersey for trafficking heroin between Sicily and the United States for distribution via pizza parlours.
Four men already sentenced for their role in the Sindona kidnapping affair of 1979, were cleared of complicity with the Mafia.

Sindona went missing for three months when he was wanted by U.S. authorities over the collapse of the Franklin National Bank, the biggest U.S. bank failure, and claimed he had been kidnapped by extremists.
One of the four cleared on Tuesday, Sindona's personal doctor Joseph Miceli Crimi, shot the banker in the leg to try to lend credibility to the kidnapping story.
Sindona was later convicted of jumping bail and sentenced to 25 years for fraud, perjury and simulating his own kidnapping.
He was extradited to Italy and died in prison in 1986 after drinking a cup of coffee laced with poison.
Falcone and Borsellino, Italy's star anti-Mafia judges, launched a series of investigations which culminated in the first mass Mafia trials of the mid-1980s.
The Mafia killed both men within months of each other in bomb attacks in Sicily in 1992.
